Comments: RATSCAT (Radar Target Scatter) is an rader cross-section (RCS) measurement facility that tests radar reflectivity, mainly for military stealth and defense applications.
Aeronautical IFF, gnd2air is a ground-to-air IFF system where ground stations interrogate aircraft, which respond with coded signals to identify as friendly or not.
DME (Distance Measuring Equipment) is an aviation system that helps aircraft determine their distance from a ground-based transponder.

Aeronautical IFF, air2gnd is an air-to-ground Identification Friend or Foe (IFF) system, where aircraft transmit identification signals to ground stations, helping distinguish friendly from potentially hostile aircraft.
GPS, Galileo, and GLONASS L5 refer to signals from Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) that operate in the L5 frequency band.
The VLA modem is a data transmission system used at the Very Large Array (VLA) to relay signals, control commands, or monitor RFI in radio astronomy operations.
The Tethered Aerostat Radar System (TARS) Pulsed Radar is a balloon-mounted radar used by the U.S. government for border surveillance, early warning, and target tracking.
GLONASS L2 is a 1246 MHz signal from Russia’s GNSS, used for military and high-precision applications.
A navigation signal transmitted by China’s BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS).

White Sands Missile Range (WSMR) is a U.S. military testing and research facility located in New Mexico, USA. It is the largest military installation in the United States, covering over 8,200 square kilometers (3,200 square miles).

GPS L3 NUDET is a classified military signal transmitted by GPS satellites as part of the U.S. Nuclear Detonation Detection System (NUDET). It operates at 1381.05 MHz and is used for global nuclear explosion monitoring.
Fort Sumner, New Mexico, hosts NASA’s Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility (CSBF), launching high-altitude research balloons up to 42 km for astrophysics, atmospheric studies, and technology testing.
Test telemetry transmits real-time data from military equipment during testing to monitor performance, system status, and environmental conditions for validation.
INMARSAT (International Maritime Satellite Organization) operates a global satellite network providing communication services for maritime, aviation, and military users.

GPS L1 is the primary signal transmitted by Global Positioning System (GPS) satellites for civilian and military navigation. It operates at 1575.42 MHz and is widely used for positioning, timing, and geolocation applications.

GLONASS L1 is one of the main signals transmitted by GLONASS (Global Navigation Satellite System), Russia’s counterpart to GPS. It operates at 1602 MHz ± 0.5625 MHz and is used for civilian and military navigation.
IRIDIUM is a global satellite communication network providing voice, data, and tracking services via a constellation of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites.

The 2nd harmonic of VLA radios refers to unintended radio frequency emissions at twice the fundamental frequency of communication or electronic systems used at the Very Large Array (VLA). These harmonics can cause radio frequency interference (RFI) in sensitive radio astronomy observations.]

The GOES (Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite) system, operated by NOAA, provides real-time weather monitoring, storm tracking, and climate data from geostationary orbit (~35,786 km altitude).

A NOAA weather satellite is a U.S. government satellite operated by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) for weather forecasting, climate monitoring, and environmental observations.
